title: Filters and ultrafilters: large subsets, maximality, and examples
summary: Consistent notions of large subsets extend to ultrafilters that decide every complement pair.
abstract: Every tail of the natural numbers contains all but finitely many numbers, but the intersection of all the tails is empty. A filter records a notion of largeness that is preserved by enlarging sets and taking finite intersections. An ultrafilter goes further, declaring exactly one of each subset and its complement large. Assuming choice, every filter extends to an ultrafilter. Starting with the sets that omit only finitely many natural numbers gives an ultrafilter that contains no finite set: it decides every subset without concentrating on a single number.
